title: Group Employees by Email Domain
statement:
A company stores a list of employees, each with a name and an email address. The **department** of an employee is the part of the email address after the `@` symbol (for example, `example.com` for `john@example.com`).

Group the employees by department and print every department together with its employees.

The output must be canonical:

- Departments are printed in increasing alphabetical order of their name (plain character-code comparison).
- Inside a department, employees are printed in the order they appear in the input (two employees may share the same name; print each of them).

For each department print a line `Department: <name>`, followed by one line `  Employee: <employee name>` (two leading spaces) for each of its employees.
inputFormat:
The first line contains the integer `n`.
Each of the next `n` lines contains the employee's name and email address separated by a space.
outputFormat: For each department, a line `Department: <name>` followed by its employees, one per line, as `  Employee: <name>` (two leading spaces).
constraints: Names consist of letters only, length 1 to 10

Each email contains exactly one `@`; the part before it is 1 to 10 characters from lowercase letters, digits and `.`, and the domain after it is 1 to 15 characters from lowercase letters, digits and `.`

examples.input:
4
John john@example.com
Jane jane@example.com
Jim jim@example2.com
Jill jill@example.com
examples.output:
Department: example.com
  Employee: John
  Employee: Jane
  Employee: Jill
Department: example2.com
  Employee: Jim
examples.explanation: Three people use example.com and one uses example2.com. Departments are sorted alphabetically and employees keep their input order.

examples.input:
3
Zed z@b.org
Ann a@a.org
Bob b@b.org
examples.output:
Department: a.org
  Employee: Ann
Department: b.org
  Employee: Zed
  Employee: Bob
examples.explanation: a.org sorts before b.org even though b.org appears first in the input. Zed comes before Bob inside b.org because he was listed first.
